data.name: Fayek
data.gender_notes: Fayek is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The one who possesses or owns. The name Fayek carries the meaning “Owner, possessor” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Fayek usually hope their child will grow to embody owner, possessor and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine possession of one's abilities and talents
data.etymology: Fayek belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Owner, possessor.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Fayek total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_arabic.name: فايك
in_arabic.meaning: اسم يعني العدل والإنصاف والثبات في الدين
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم الفايك من أصل عربي يعود إلى العصر الجاهلي، ويستخدم في العديد من السياقات لوصف المُثبت الدين، والذي يُعرف بالعدل والإنصاف في الحياة. ويُعتبر اسم الفايك من أسماء الله الحسنى، ويُستخدم في القرآن الكريم، ويُحتفظ به في التراث الإسلامي كإسم لمن يُحافظ على قيم الإسلام، ويُعيش حياته وفقاً للشريعة. ويُعد اسم الفايك من أهم الأسماء الإسلامية في العصر الحديث، ويُميز الفرد الذي يحمل هذا الاسم بالثبات والإنصاف في الدين والحياه.

in_english.name: Fayek
in_english.meaning: Name meaning justice, fairness and steadfastness in faith
in_english.long_meaning: Fayek is an Arabic name that dates back to the pre-Islamic era, and is used to describe individuals who uphold the values of Islam and live a life of justice and fairness. As a name of God, Fayek is mentioned in the Quran and is revered in Islamic tradition as a symbol of virtue and righteousness. In modern times, the name Fayek has become a popular choice among Muslims, symbolizing the values of justice, fairness, and devotion to one's faith.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Fayek" or its variations (Fayek, Faiq, Fahik, Faik, etc.) in the Arabic culture is believed to represent an individual of power and wealth. It connotes ownership and control, and is often associated with those who hold positions of influence and authority. This may include business leaders, political figures, and religious scholars.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Fayek" can be interpreted to represent one who is in possession of divine wisdom and knowledge. In the Islamic tradition, it is said that Allah (God) blesses His chosen servants with understanding and insight, making them "owners" of knowledge and truth. These individuals, through their exemplary lives and actions, inspire others to seek knowledge, wisdom, and spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Owner, possessor" symbolizes The one who possesses or owns. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Fayek serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of owner, possessor.

historical_references.context: Ibn Battuta mentions a man named Fayek, who was a leading figure in the city of Qayrawan, Tunisia during his travels. Fayek was renowned for his extensive knowledge, generosity, and hospitality towards travelers.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Maqrizi's 'The History of the Prophets and Kings of Egypt' The name Fayek carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Al-Maqrizi records the name of a Mamluk Sultan named Fayek, who ruled Egypt from 1386 to 1389 AD. He was a member of the Circularian Mamluks, known for their military prowess and political power in Egypt.
